values: Schedule of Compliance, Delta-BHC Study (Part I.B), including the immediately following sentence on plan content and post-approval quarterly sampling during permit years 2–5
Distinction between administrative plan-submission obligations and monitoring requirements that entail sample collection and analysis

grounding.excerpt: The permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for approval.

The plan must also include any use of delta-BHC at the facility, if any. Once approved, the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit.

rationale: The six-month deadline grammatically attaches to the administrative act of submitting a detailed plan for agency approval, not to sample collection or field testing. The infinitive phrase "to test for Delta-BHC at the source water intake" modifies the plan's content (a plan describing how testing will be conducted), rather than imposing an immediate monitoring obligation within that window. The permit then separately imposes a distinct post-approval monitoring requirement—"Once approved, the permittee must collect and analyze samples"—with explicit timing during permit years 2 through 5. This textual sequencing establishes the distinction in value 2: the Schedule of Compliance clause imposes an administrative plan-submission obligation within six months, while the sample-collection-and-analysis obligation is deferred until after approval and does not apply during the plan-submission period.
